title: Merge two sorted lists
prompt:
Write merge_sorted(a, b) that takes two lists, each already sorted from small to large, and returns one new sorted list with all the items.
Do it in one pass without calling sorted() on the combined list.
hints: Think of two queues of people, each sorted by height. Who goes next into the combined line?
Keep a position in each list. Compare the two items at those positions, take the smaller, and move that position forward. What happens when one list runs out?
Plan: i = j = 0; while both lists have items left, compare a[i] and b[j] and append the smaller; afterwards, whatever remains of either list is already sorted, so add it all at the end.

edge_hints.empty: If one list is empty the answer is just the other one. Check your loop condition and what you add after it.
edge_hints.duplicates: Equal items are fine; make sure none get lost or doubled when the two sides are equal.
